correctness.rationale: The conditional identities follow by applying invariance to arbitrary smooth antiderivatives of \(x\) and \(z\): \(L\Phi(x)=a\Phi'(x)(y-x)\) and \(L\Psi(z)=\Psi'(z)(hx^2-cz)\). An independent symbolic calculation verified that for \(F=-hxy+(h/2)x^2+bz-(k/2)z^2\), \(LF=kc z^2-bc z-ah(y-x)^2\), giving the exact completed-square identity. Equality forces \(y=x\) and \(z\in\{0,b/k\}\) almost surely; invariance then restricts support to \((0,0,0)\) and \((\pm\sqrt{bc/(hk)},\pm\sqrt{bc/(hk)},b/k)\). The strict excursion and sign-change consequences follow because a non-equilibrium invariant measure makes the nonnegative defect term positive while the invariant mean of \(y-x\) is zero.
correctness.risk: Statements are for compact invariant probabilities; existence of a particular chaotic physical/SRB measure is not asserted.

value.rationale: The theorem gives exact global stationary constraints, a sharp equilibrium-height defect, and a rigidity/equilibrium classification for an established chaotic model. These are structurally motivated observables and turn a local threshold \(b/k\) into a necessary excursion law for every non-equilibrium compact invariant measure.
value.risk: The formulas are model-specific and do not by themselves establish existence or uniqueness of a physical invariant measure.

final_claim: For every compact invariant probability measure of the Liu system \(\dot x=a(y-x),\ \dot y=x(b-kz),\ \dot z=hx^2-cz\) with positive parameters, \(\mathbb E[y\mid x]=x\), \(\mathbb E[x^2\mid z]=(c/h)z\), and \[\mathbb E[(z-b/(2k))^2]=b^2/(4k^2)+(ah/(kc))\mathbb E[(y-x)^2].\] Equality occurs exactly for convex mixtures of the three equilibria; every non-equilibrium compact invariant measure assigns positive mass to \(z>b/k\) and to both signs of \(y-x\).
limitations: No ergodicity or SRB property is assumed or concluded.
The theorem concerns compact invariant probability measures only.
